title: Juhi Chawla Closes Apple's Diwali Film 'Step Into the Light,' Shot on iPhone 18 Pro
excerpt: The Hindi-language festive film, made with Raw Mango and set at Rajasthan's Tijara Fort, revives her 1994 song 'Roop Suhana Lagta Hai' in a folk arrangement.
body:
• Apple released its Diwali campaign 'Step Into the Light' on November 4, filmed entirely on the iPhone 18 Pro in collaboration with Indian fashion label Raw Mango.
  • Juhi Chawla makes a closing appearance in the film, set at Tijara Fort, a restored 19th-century palace in Rajasthan.
  • The soundtrack is a folk interpretation of 'Roop Suhana Lagta Hai,' Anu Malik's song from her 1994 film The Gentleman.
  • The film is available on Apple's global Instagram account and Apple India's YouTube channel.

Apple has released a new Diwali film, 'Step Into the Light,' featuring actor Juhi Chawla and created in collaboration with Indian fashion label Raw Mango, according to afaqs!. The film is part of Apple's Shot on iPhone series and was filmed entirely on the iPhone 18 Pro.

Directed by Raw Mango founder Sanjay Garg, the film is set at Tijara Fort, a restored 19th-century palace in Rajasthan, and uses dance, traditional textiles and lighting to depict Diwali — the year's darkest night turned, in the campaign's framing, into a call to step into the light. Dancers wear saris highlighting Chanderi, Mashru and Varanasi brocades.

The 1994 connection

The film is built around a folk interpretation of 'Roop Suhana Lagta Hai,' the Anu Malik song from the 1994 Hindi film The Gentleman, which starred Chiranjeevi and Chawla. Bollywood Hungama reported that Chawla's appearance comes in the closing frames, dressed in festive Raw Mango ensembles — a surprise cameo that ties the technology showcase directly to her own filmography.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfXhEy8ssE9/

The camera claim

The production was shot in low light to demonstrate the phone's camera. Campaign coverage notes the iPhone 18 Pro's 48MP Fusion main camera, variable aperture — described as a first for iPhone, with six laser-cut blades adapting to lighting and depth of field — and smart focus tracking. The point of the Shot on iPhone format is that no other camera was used; the fort's diya-lit sequences are the demonstration.

How to watch

The film was released on November 4 on Apple's global Instagram account and Apple India's YouTube channel, ahead of Diwali, with a behind-the-scenes film following on Instagram Stories showing Garg at work on set. For diaspora viewers, it is a short festive watch that pairs a 1990s Bollywood memory with three handloom traditions — and it is also a marker of how central the Indian festive calendar has become to global technology marketing: Apple built its Diwali film around an Indian label, an Indian fort and a Hindi song, and shot the whole production on the phone it is selling.
